A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CPCP research work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–C are readable and can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on eight regression benchmarks, including baseline comparisons and ALD, clipping, and mixing analyses in Section 6 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v4 reports original benchmark comparisons, additional coverage diagnostics, a multihead control, and bandwidth sensitivity results in Section 6 and Appendix A.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same noncrossing three-head network, finite-difference density weights, weighted central-head fine-tuning, rectified conformalization, and optional clipping/mixing. Explicit freezing instructions in v4 clarify the existing procedure; correcting the additive constant in Equation 17 does not change its optimizer.

E1.justification: Both evaluate Bike, Diamond, Gas Turbine, Naval, SGEMM, Superconductivity, Transcoding, and WEC on the same scalar or multivariate regression tasks. Appendix A.1 retains the dataset populations, dimensions, sample counts, and preprocessing.

E2.justification: v4 adds RCP-MultiHead, which co-trains three quantiles and uses the central estimate for RCP, to the comparisons in Appendix A.5. The existing comparator methods, including both PLCP group configurations, remain.

E3.justification: v4 adds classification-based L1-ERT and L2-ERT evaluation using logistic regression, replaces secondary MSCE clustering at K=50 with K=30, and introduces bandwidth and multihead control settings. K=10, 90% target coverage, and the data splits remain. Its main PLCP rows match appendix G=20 results, although Appendix A.2 still specifies G=50.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained ALD and clipping/mixing analyses, v4 tests whether three-head co-training alone explains the gains and evaluates bandwidths 0.01 and 0.05 alongside the default 0.02, with and without stabilization. These add direct mechanism controls and sensitivity evidence across the benchmarks.

E5.justification: Both versions specify 20 Monte Carlo repetitions and report mean plus standard deviation. No additional run-count, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing practice is introduced; changed numerical standard deviations belong to the result revisions.

E6.justification: Existing MSCE, WSC, and volume results change broadly, and v4 adds ERT, multihead, and bandwidth result entries. For example, CPCP (Clip+Mix) Bike WSC changes from 0.8932 ± 0.0142 to 0.8882 ± 0.0250 in Table 2. The K=30 MSCE results replace K=50 results and cannot establish a same-setting performance change.

T1.justification: Assumption 5.1 narrows the exponent range from (0,1] to [1/3,1]. Appendix B.3.4 restores missing 1/(2δ) factors in the denominator-stability argument and derives d≤4s for the Hölder instantiation. v4 also restores the 1/2 coefficient in Equation 12, adds the missing constant in Equation 17, and revises finite-sample bound calculations. These affect mathematical reasoning and theorem applicability.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same headline claims: a sharper density-weighted surrogate for conditional coverage error, the CPCP framework, non-asymptotic excess-risk analysis, and empirical conditional-coverage improvements. The added experiments support these existing contributions.

C2.justification: v4 explicitly explains the slower-rate limitation below ν=1/3, the associated dimensionality restriction, and its motivation for clipping; it removes the earlier ReLU applicability example. Section 6.1 additionally interprets the multihead ablation as supporting the core methodology and discusses flexibility beyond neural quantile regressors.

D1.justification: v4 adds a code-access link on its first page and documents the new multihead control, alternative bandwidth values, and logistic-regression implementation of ERT. The existing architecture, calibration proportions, and clipping/mixing defaults remain. Repository contents cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v4 adds Feldman, Bates, and Romano (2021), citing orthogonal quantile regression when discussing conditional-coverage limitations. It expands its use of the already-cited Braun et al. (2025b) through ERT diagnostics. The broader positioning relative to RCP and other conformal methods remains.

P1.justification: v4 makes localized revisions to the preliminaries, experimental description, results interpretation, and proof explanations, while standardizing heading capitalization and citation/reference style. The overall narrative, section sequence, and appendix organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v4 adds an L1-ERT main table and L1-/L2-ERT appendix tables, expands comparison rows, groups the main tables together, and relocates Algorithm 2. These extend and rearrange existing displays; Figure 1 and the basic table design remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 strengthens validation through the multihead control, bandwidth sensitivity tests, and complementary coverage diagnostics, while correcting mathematical expressions and making the convergence-rate restriction explicit. Reporting inconsistencies limit the gain: the main PLCP configuration conflicts with Appendix A.2, and Gaussian-Scoring's WEC L1-ERT differs between Tables 3 and 8 (0.0996 versus 0.0691). Overall, the added scrutiny and precision provide a useful but qualified improvement.
